title: Former DOGE Engineer Is Now Back in Government
content: Sahil Lavingia, previously a DOGE operative at the Department of Veterans Affairs, is now a career employee at the IRS. He said at WIRED’s Big Interview event that he expects to work there 10 years.

title: ‘Signalgate’ Inspector General Report Wants Just One Change to Avoid a Repeat Debacle
content: The United States Inspector General report reviewing Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s text messaging mess recommends a single change to keep classified material secure.

title: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie: Past Leaders Took the City ‘for Granted’
content: People like to rag on the Bay Area, but mayor Daniel Lurie believes there’s no better place in the world than San Francisco.

title: Trump Wants to Trade Fuel Economy for Cheaper Cars. But It Might Not Work
content: By rolling back auto industry fuel efficiency goals, US president Donald Trump hopes to make new cars cheaper. But prices won’t drop for years, and consumers will spend more on gas in the meantime.

title: Can AI Look at Your Retina and Diagnose Alzheimer’s? Eric Topol Hopes So
content: The author of Super Agers believes AI could bring big changes to the world of medicine.

title: Cloudflare Has Blocked 416 Billion AI Bot Requests Since July 1
content: Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince claims the internet infrastructure company’s efforts to block AI crawlers are already seeing big results.

title: Anthropic’s Daniela Amodei Believes the Market Will Reward Safe AI
content: The Trump administration might think regulation is killing the AI industry, but Anthropic president Daniela Amodei disagrees.

title: What Happens When Your Coworkers Are AI Agents
content: In this episode of Uncanny Valley, we talk to writer Evan Ratliff about how he created a small startup made entirely of AI employees—and what his findings reveal about the reality of an agentic future.

title: Jon M. Chu Says AI Couldn’t Have Made One of the Best Moments in ‘Wicked’
content: The Wicked: For Good director says being able to improvise on set allows for the kind of moments that are hard for machines to make.

title: The 67 Best Movies on Disney+, WIRED’s Picks (December 2025)
content: Madame Web, Love+War, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps are just a few of the movies you should be watching on Disney+ this month.

title: FBI Says DC Pipe Bomb Suspect Brian Cole Kept Buying Bomb Parts After January 6
content: The 30-year-old Virginia resident evaded capture for years after authorities discovered pipe bombs planted near buildings in Washington, DC, the day before the January 6, 2021, Capitol attack.

title: AMD CEO Lisa Su Says Concerns About an AI Bubble Are Overblown
content: Lisa Su leads Nvidia’s biggest rival in the AI chip market. When asked at WIRED’s Big Interview event if AI is a bubble, the company’s CEO said, “Emphatically, from my perspective, no.”

title: A New Anonymous Phone Carrier Lets You Sign Up With Nothing but a Zip Code
content: Privacy stalwart Nicholas Merrill spent a decade fighting an FBI surveillance order. Now he wants to sell you phone service—without knowing almost anything about you.

title: ByteDance and DeepSeek Are Placing Very Different AI Bets
content: The diverging path of China’s two leading AI players shows where the country’s artificial intelligence industry is headed.

title: InnAIO AI Translator T10 Review: Feature-Loaded but Needs Work
content: The InnAIO T10 clips magnetically to the back of your phone, but it needs further development to be worth the money.
